scope: 44 finite admission/algorithm/filesystem duties, bounded executed witnesses and seven proposed repair/qualification packets; planning only

packets.title: Localize and repair accepted flat-expression stack abort
packets.classification: demonstrated valid-source native-debug defect; repair mechanism pending localization
packets.writer_release: Localization first; release only the demonstrated responsible traversal/clone/drop owner and its directly affected callers, not all listed files or a structural redesign. Parser writer only if separately selected admission policy is necessary.
packets.acceptance: Retain 64/256/512 positive controls and all six exact flat sources; isolate failing analysis/emission/ownership stage in supervised subprocesses. Accepted valid sources check/compile/drop normally; independently execute emitted legal sums (64 through3000) and preserve left associativity, precedence and effect/evaluation order. If an explicit refusal policy is selected, assert its exact diagnostic before unsafe downstream work, without silently converting currently supported forms to unsupported. Qualify malformed/recovery and member/postfix siblings separately. No release/host threshold inferred from debug neighbors.
packets.policy: No chosen structural-depth budget or parser/arena redesign. Compare iterative owner traversal, ownership cleanup and explicit admission fairly after localization; consequential limits/support changes require verified-context JEV and recorded decision.

packets.title: Qualify executable internal-fault wording
packets.classification: documented guarantee exceeds actual unwind boundary
packets.acceptance: Describe caught unwinding panic E7005/exit2 precisely; state abort/stack-overflow and default allocation-error limits, and that public APIs inherit no executable boundary. Existing forced-unwind control remains2/E7005; no new exhaustion test. Comment/document repair must not claim stack-defect remediation.
packets.policy: No change to panic strategy, abort containment or library API support.

packets.title: Qualify bounded LSP header/body admission
packets.classification: demonstrated allocation timing and absent header budget; resource policy gap, no exhaustion witness
packets.acceptance: Before selecting a header cap/error recovery, define supported line/aggregate/count budgets and malformed-frame lifecycle. Verify below/at/above selected budgets with short supervised inputs and body read observer; preserved valid extensions, legal Content-Length and actual initialized framed sessions succeed. If body allocation becomes incremental, prove allocation follows actual arrival while retaining the existing64MiB maximum and exact accepted bytes. Keep duplicate-last-wins and current server continuation policy unless explicitly revised.
packets.policy: Cap values and resynchronization/reset/close choices are proposals; consequential refusal/lifecycle changes need verified-context JEV. No memory/RSS/slow-client or portable exhaustion guarantee.

packets.title: Remove build metadata missing-path rebuilds
packets.classification: observed unnecessary repeated rebuild; stale-hash hypothesis falsified in tested profile
packets.acceptance: Resolve actual Git metadata paths for ordinary, detached, packed-ref and linked-worktree layouts; independent consumer commit remains current after commits/ref changes. Repeated unchanged supported layouts do not rebuild due solely to nonexistent watched paths. Preserve tarball/noGit/failingGit unknown fallback; use disposable repository fixtures. Count complete watcher/helper closure before claiming simplification.
packets.policy: No dependency selected; no stale-version bug claim or broad performance/other-Cargo guarantee.

packets.title: Qualify renderer and output failure lifecycle
packets.classification: source-only process/reaping and resource leads; no new witnessed defect
packets.acceptance: Use disposable fixed-argv renderer children to qualify early stdin closure, child exit/signal, pending wait/reap, finite output and explicit timeout/error controls; retain real stdout BrokenPipe result semantics. Establish supported timeout/capture expectations before repair. Preserve filesystem C04F behavior and distinguish renderer stub/interface from installed rendering.
packets.policy: No arbitrary subprocess timeout/output cap or all-sink resilience selected; qualify before releasing production writer.

packets.title: Define source/carrier representability and width qualification
packets.classification: source/invariant policy gaps; not reproduced valid-input crash
packets.writer_release: Split by owning boundary after a supported obligation is selected; no common blanket budget or giant input experiment.
packets.acceptance: Select and test centralized representability obligations with small boundary helpers; qualify actual used catalog signature matching, field reuse and representative finite graph/ICU/output widths before claims. Distinguish accepted parsed wire/source from forged public carriers and measured workload from source complexity. Preserve exact values, diagnostics/multiplicity, mappings and complete consumers.
packets.policy: No >4GiB/OOM/flood execution, source/global/graph/output limit, public invariant guarantee or dependency selected.

packets.title: Reuse session-history ownership and preserve host/file qualification gates
packets.classification: existing observed retention plus host coverage gate; no new filesystem blocker
packets.acceptance: Reuse ED-R06 rather than create a competing history API: preserve immutable live/checked SourceIds while qualifying bounded session ownership and historical lint work with representative edits. Keep native4750 fixture-unqualified state explicit and prior Linux execution separately pinned; qualify another supported host only when needed.
packets.policy: No reclamation/cache/history or host policy selected. C04F requested-entry replacement, noop, modes, partial progress and trusted-parent limits remain accepted.
